observations: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show the same keyboard from slightly different angles, wrapped in clear plastic.
The keyboard has 61 keys (standard piano layout), with white and black keys visible.
The front panel includes a central display screen, control knobs, buttons, and a speaker grille.
The keyboard appears to be in used condition, with some visible wear on the plastic wrap and surface.
No power cord, stand, or accessories are visible in the photos.
The seller claims it is a 'London used keyboard with super sounds' and 'All keys and buttons working'.

claims.claim: Quality London used keyboard with super sounds
claims.evidence: No photo shows this clearly enough to read.
No video or photo shows the keyboard powered on or keys being played. The display is off in both photos.
No adapter is visible in either photo. The seller's text claims it, but it is not shown.

claims.claim: Bought from the UK, no dead key, no crackle.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: Keyboard may not power on or keys may not function
risks.proof: Video clip showing the keyboard powered on, display lit, and keys being played.
Photo showing all included accessories laid out next to the keyboard.

risks.risk: Internal damage or dead keys not visible in photos
risks.proof: Close-up video of keys being pressed and sound produced, or a test of all keys.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having potential dead keys

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powered on and playing a few notes to verify keys and buttons work.
Photo showing the power adapter and any included accessories.
Close-up of the display screen and any labels or serial numbers.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
